items.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004
items.q: I thought it would be neat to get like Daniel Lanois or somebody to help us paint a whole different sonic picture

ctx.x: That’s good. I think that’s a luxury.

Yeah I mean we’ve had pressure on us to have outside producers and early on I think Future Man was the one who didn’t want to have any part of it. Because he had had some bad experiences, Victor and Future Man, the Wooten brothers. There’s five of them. And they had a big deal at a certain point on Arista records and a fellow named Kashif who © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

produced I guess Whitney Houston and some other people and was producing them. And some bad things happened. Like they came in one day and Vic’s parts had been replaced by another bass player or a keyboard, or things like that. And they felt very taken advantage of and they were very suspicious of producers. And so for Future Man, who is doing something very unusual, he didn’t like the idea of some other person having a say about what he did. He was very un-into it at that point. And if it was the wrong producer…
